narration.text: For forty years a lamp on a headland was lit at dusk. It turned all night above water nobody else was watching.
Before he slept, the keeper wrote the hour and the weather down. The log was a condition of the job, and he met it.
A slatted white box on the grass held his thermometers. He read them at the same hour, whatever the sea was doing.
A century later his logbook stands closed on an archive shelf. Its columns became a record of the water itself; kept things outlive their reason.
